title: Opinion on why robotics lacks applications
why: Argues most robotics experiments add little reusable knowledge; the real gains came from better batteries, electronics, and manufacturing, not new ideas.

title: Reflections from a long-time programmer
why: Personal reflections that programming languages matter less than what you build; no concrete technical lesson.

title: Practical rules for deploying services ops trust
why: Ship init.d scripts with start, stop, and status; drop root after setup; use config files; provide deb or rpm packaging; fix bugs ops reports.

title: Fake Hacker News front page joke
why: A nostalgic parody of Hacker News front page; entertaining but no technical lesson.

title: Why experts miss usability pain in their tools
why: Enthusiasts underestimate the learning curve of their own tools; Wikidata's query counts and SPARQL and RDF complexity deter ordinary developers.

title: Critique of Stack Overflow's editing culture
why: Opinionated argument about editors, askers, and answerers; no substantive technical content.

title: Life advice list from an old man
why: Personal, political, and opinionated life advice with no technical substance.

title: Why bitcoin mining continues despite losses
why: Mining difficulty stays decoupled from price; miners either bet on future price or are stuck with sunk hardware, mining at a loss.

title: Personal memories of coal heating in Britain
why: Nostalgic personal account of coal heating and childhood chores with no lesson for a technical reader.

title: Comparing Flow and TypeScript issue counts
why: Opinion based on counting open and closed GitHub issues; the ratio does not show project quality.

title: Why React, Next, and JAMstack exist
why: Raw DOM is hard for stateful UIs; React offers composable components, while frameworks add routing, state persistence, and static builds.

title: Launch post asking for feedback on a note app
why: Solicits feedback on a personal app with a motivation story; no transferable technical insight.

title: Speculation on Apple's car ambitions
why: Speculative opinion that CarPlay is the real goal; no verifiable technical content.

title: Argument about whether ideas have value
why: Back-and-forth argument over founders needing technical partners; no lesson beyond personal opinion.

title: Why repair rules conflict with hardware trust
why: Replaceable secure components can let malicious parties swap in hostile parts; a trusted hardware chain is hard to open to third-party repair.

title: Personal account of job hunting at 50
why: Personal career frustration about interview bars and ageism; no technical lesson.

title: Examples of failed 1970 environmental predictions
why: Political argument built on cherry-picked wrong predictions; it does not explain climate science.

title: Personal account of sleep problems with CFS
why: Personal health anecdote about sleep disruption with no generalizable lesson for other readers.

title: Why starving tumors is hard in practice
why: Angiogenesis inhibitors and starving cancers also hit other fast-turnover tissues, and tumors switch to anaerobic glucose metabolism to resist therapy.

title: Why soft-serve machines lock out
why: Machines boil dairy nightly and must be torn down every 14 days; missed heat cycles or expired timers trigger lockouts that cause most service calls.

title: Algorithmic trading is execution, not HFT
why: Algorithmic trading means automatically executing a large order over time to limit market impact, not the speed-based high-frequency strategies critics target.

title: Opinion on managing frontend app complexity
why: Mostly a survey of past frontend tools and personal preference for React; little actionable technical explanation.

title: Personal recommendations for US checking accounts
why: Anecdotal bank recommendations for a specific time and country; the products and terms have since changed.

title: Contested opinion on genetic differences
why: Politically charged opinion on race and genetics with no rigorous evidence presented.

title: Rant about founders feeling guilty
why: Opinionated essay on startup ethics and social value; argument rather than teaching.

title: Rant about founders feeling guilty
why: Opinionated essay on startup ethics and social value; argument rather than teaching.

title: What working inside Google is really like
why: Visible codebase, universal code review, and internal mailing lists trade politics for transparency; big-company processes scale but are not utopian.

title: Letter to a principal about academics
why: Personal letter about a student's workload and school performance; no technical lesson.

title: Rant defending PyCharm over vim
why: Personal workflow preference argued through a long day of coding; opinion rather than a transferable technique.

title: Letter to the FDA about DNA access
why: Advocacy letter with speculation about insurance industry motives; no technical explanation.

title: Creating a local Windows account during setup
why: Windows 10 setup hides the local-account option; entering a wrong password for a Microsoft account reveals the create-offline-account path.

title: Rant defending Google against critics
why: Emotional argument comparing Google and Apple openness; no technical content.

title: Why the youtube-dl DMCA claim is weak
why: Section 1201(a)(2) covers bypassing access controls; a user with valid credentials who misuses access has not circumvented anything, per court precedent.

title: Curated machine learning reading path
why: Metacademy for orientation, then Ng's CS229, ISL, and PRML or Murphy for depth, presented as a choose-your-own-adventure path.

title: Dropbox as a photo and media platform
why: Consumer-behavior opinion about sharing and encryption; the post is mainly argument about product market fit.

title: macOS is hard to use without a mouse
why: Argues macOS menus and dialogs need the mouse; the experience claim is subjective and gives no technique.

title: Why parties converge and elections stay close
why: Parties act as brands that simplify voter choice; Hotelling's law pushes them toward the middle, yielding narrow majorities and close elections.

title: Defense of Facebook for shy users
why: Personal argument for Facebook's social value; opinion rather than explanation.

title: Skeptical take on NFT tweet auction
why: Opinion that NFT certificates confer little ownership of a publicly visible tweet; argument without technical teaching.

title: Why Reddit centralizes hobby communities
why: Personal opinion on Reddit's value for finding communities; no technical or factual lesson.

title: Argument against streaming content quotas
why: Speculative policy argument about unintended consequences of local content quotas; opinion rather than evidence.

title: How one dinner plan touches many trackers
why: Email, search, analytics on a restaurant site, calendar, maps, and voice assistants each pass data to Google, even when you leave its services.

title: Critique of lean FIRE planning
why: Personal opinion that lean FIRE plans ignore life changes; argument rather than a worked financial method.

title: Humorous story about a Home Depot mix-up
why: A light personal anecdote about an accidental self-checkout error; entertaining but no lesson.

title: Argument that dystopia terms are outdated
why: Literary opinion arguing that fascism and tyranny framings are dated; a debate about rhetoric, not a technical lesson.

title: Satirical story about a startup bust
why: Satirical narrative speculating about a startup crash; entertaining but not informative.

title: Skeptical take on an automated camera product
why: Opinion questioning use cases for an unattended camera; mostly a product critique.

title: Doubts about self-driving in chaotic cities
why: Anecdotal argument that autonomous cars struggle in messy traffic and poor infrastructure; opinion rather than explanation.

title: Why Stack Overflow is a community resource
why: Many people search rather than ask, so answers are written once and read by thousands; SO chose CC licensing after Experts-Exchange paywalled community content.

title: Advice on high-value consulting careers
why: Motivational career advice about networks and timing; mostly opinion without concrete, checkable steps.

title: How card chargebacks drain merchant funds
why: Chargebacks provisionally reverse transactions and debit the processor's funds from the merchant; processors hold reserves to cover losses if consumers win.

title: Opinion on gender roles and birth rates
why: Contested opinion about family and society with no evidence beyond personal observation.

title: Why doctors undermine hospital security
why: Physicians resisting passwords and MFA, combined with overrides, let a phished credential lead to a hospital network breach and wire fraud.

title: Why equity can't replace salary
why: Startup equity is worth nothing until an exit and landlords don't accept options, so equity works as an incentive on top of salary, not a substitute.

title: Opinion on expensive keyboard hobby
why: Enthusiast opinion that premium keyboards show diminishing returns; subjective taste rather than explanation.

title: Advice to walk away from a cofounder dispute
why: Personal advice on a cofounder conflict; opinion-driven guidance without verifiable technical or factual content.

title: Why tilted solar arrays can't beat optimal
why: Independent panels' energy adds linearly, so suboptimally angled panels never beat one optimally oriented panel; the claimed gain is an experimental error.

title: Open questions about the lab leak theory
why: Speculative argument listing open questions about COVID origins; contested and not a settled technical lesson.

title: Integrated math versus the staged US sequence
why: California's plan replaces year-by-year algebra then geometry with integrated applied courses, a structure common in European curricula, adding statistics and probability.

title: Personal story of jumping between IT jobs
why: Personal career narrative about contract jobs and tech support; no transferable technical lesson.

title: Opinion on keeping old cars longer
why: Mechanic's opinion on car age and safety tradeoffs; anecdotal and argumentative rather than a practical guide.

title: Worry about cost-of-living pay cuts
why: Personal concern about geographic pay policies at a tech company; opinion without technical substance.

title: Deep learning as compressed memorization
why: Argues ML reduces to memorizing data with varying compression: kNN has none, neural nets compress, so the value lies mainly in the data.

title: Small machines versus one industrial napkin line
why: Matching one industrial machine needs 175 cheap machines and 700 workers; per-unit power and labor costs make small machines lose on economics.

title: Why small p-value studies make weak foundations
why: Barely significant tiny effects from underpowered studies are unreliable foundations; science should favor robust effects backed by adequate statistical power.

title: Self-hosting email has three separate layers
why: Own your domain for portability, host the mailbox if you want, but sending mail needs a stable reputable IP and ongoing monitoring, the hardest part.

title: Comparing salaries across careers
why: Informal comparison of job salaries by city; anecdotal, and the gender point is argument rather than analysis.

title: How a notary chain timestamped documents
why: Client hashes are batched into a Merkle tree; the root joins a linked hash chain, so certificates prove a document existed at a given time.

title: China's nine vaccines and real-world data
why: China developed nine COVID vaccines, not one; CoronaVac showed 66% symptomatic and 86% death protection in Chilean real-world data.

title: Personal account of UK computing education
why: Personal story of limited computing courses in school and college; no transferable lesson for technical readers.

title: Moral argument about click farms
why: Moral and economic argument about spam and desperation; opinion rather than explanation of how the industry works.

title: Hiring by small take-home coding project
why: Give a one-hour project in any language, judge clean, tested, non-overengineered code, then pair in person; this filters for talent regardless of stack years.

title: Political argument on nuclear and green deals
why: Opinion on nuclear policy and political stability over decades; a values argument rather than technical explanation.

title: Critique of hiding URL parts in Chrome
why: Argues hiding scheme and subdomain undermines security awareness; a design opinion with no new technical explanation.

title: Why solar plus resistive heat can beat heat pumps
why: Per watt, cheap panels cost far less than a heat pump's savings; direct resistive heating with solar may cost about a fifth as much, ignoring seasonal and timing factors.

title: Plea for measured debate on surveillance
why: Opinion asking for serious debate about surveillance and Snowden; argument rather than technical teaching.

title: Reverse-index docs by concept, not function
why: API references help only once you know function names; indexing docs by concept lets users discover which functions implement an idea, unlike User's Guides.

title: Opinion on retail theft and customer experience
why: Opinion that anti-theft measures alienate customers; a product-experience argument rather than a technical lesson.

title: Defense of Stack Overflow's question standards
why: Opinion defending SO's question guidelines and downvoting; it gives some tips but mostly argues a position.

title: Encryption and identity are separate certificate problems
why: Certificates bundle encryption with identity checks; cheap domain validation proves domain control, not operator trustworthiness, and EV only adds visual badges.

title: Personal account of daughters and computing
why: Parent's anecdote about children's interest in computers and games; personal, with no transferable technical lesson.

title: Wishlist for a hosted startup infrastructure
why: Wish for a turnkey hosted platform to offload ops; a request for a product rather than an explanation.

title: Letter to a principal about a student's work
why: Personal letter arguing about school board decisions and a student's academic performance; no technical lesson.

title: Rant about federal domain seizure
why: Political argument about federal power and enforcement; opinion rather than a technical explanation.

title: Check architecture before trusting benchmarks
why: Benchmark numbers matched x86 emulation under Rosetta, not native arm64; verify binaries with file and retune flags like SIMDJSON_IMPLEMENTATION_ARM64 for real results.

title: Concerns about EU interoperability rules
why: Argument that interoperability and hardware access rules could weaken encryption and enable tracking; policy opinion rather than explanation.

title: Why grids make reusable blueprints possible
why: Gridded 2D worlds make blueprints stampable and parallel, like GPU work; Satisfactory's free 3D terrain makes every build unique and hard to replicate.

title: Frustration over an underperforming hire
why: Personal frustration story about a hire and interview process; a cautionary anecdote without a clear method.

title: Startup hiring advertisement
why: Recruiting post for a stealth startup; promotional rather than informative.

title: Why TeX math typesetting is hard to replace
why: Math rendering encodes centuries of typesetting knowledge in TeX's appendix G rules; input syntax, rendering, and symbol lookup are separate problems often conflated.

title: Comparing 1984 and Brave New World
why: Literary argument that Huxley's world is less dystopian; interpretive opinion rather than an explanation a technical reader can apply.

title: Argument on why people distrust science
why: Opinion that institutions lost public trust through overconfidence; a values argument with no technical lesson.

title: Remote teams succeed through deliverable accountability
why: Top performers thrive remotely; effective managers have engineers commit to deliverables publicly, sync weekly, and pair seniors with juniors, so slips surface early.

title: Freefall survival: surface area, relaxation, aim
why: Only drag is controllable: spread out to slow, go flat until landing, relax muscles to roughly halve fatality odds, and aim for trees, soil, or snow.

title: Personal memoir about a website founder
why: Personal tribute and anecdote about a planned meeting before a founder's death; no technical lesson.

title: Argument on police and domestic disputes
why: Opinion on the limits of police intervention in domestic disputes; a policy argument rather than factual explanation.

title: Question on who reads Homer and why
why: Personal question about learning Ancient Greek and cultural attitudes to classics; asks readers for opinions rather than teaching.

title: Critique of Paul Graham's essay on bosses
why: Stylistic and ideological critique of an essay about employment; argument rather than explanation of a technique.

title: Aesthetic critique of AI-generated illustrations
why: Taste-based argument that AI art copies its training style and lacks intent; opinion rather than a technical lesson.

title: Godot versus Unity for 2D games
why: Unity needs workarounds for pixel-perfect 2D and lacks nested prefabs, while Godot uses pixel units by default and nested scenes; Unity remains strong for 3D.
